item.text:
## 1B.4 Research Note: Lula, Brazil, 2024

**Bottom line:** The 2024 record is **mostly supportive** of arms-control / nonproliferation / de-escalation in good faith. Lula’s government took concrete institutional steps on disarmament and nuclear-security governance, and Lula repeatedly endorsed dialogue and ceasefire language. The main caution is the Brazil-China Ukraine peace initiative: it was clearly de-escalatory, but Ukraine later said it was “destructive” and excluded Kyiv, which weakens the good-faith signal.

### Accepted claims

- **Claim:** Lula created a permanent Brazilian delegation to the UN Conference on Disarmament.
  - **Title:** `Decreto nº 12.237, de 25 de outubro de 2024`
  - **Publisher:** Presidência da República / Planalto
  - **Date:** October 25, 2024
  - **Recoverable URL:** https://www.planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_Ato2023-2026/2024/Decreto/D12237.htm
  - **Claim-level summary:** The decree established Brazil’s permanent delegation in Geneva’s Conference on Disarmament. That is direct, formal support for disarmament diplomacy and multilateral arms-control engagement.
  - **Question IDs:** `1B.4`; also `1B.1`

- **Claim:** Brazil’s defense establishment publicly reaffirmed support for nonproliferation, safeguards, and arms-control regimes in 2024.
  - **Title:** `GSI/PR participa da IV Conferência Internacional sobre Segurança Física Nuclear`
  - **Publisher:** Gabinete de Segurança Institucional da Presidência da República
  - **Date:** May 21, 2024
  - **Recoverable URL:** https://www.gov.br/gsi/pt-br/centrais-de-conteudo/noticias/2024/gsi-pr-participa-da-iv-conferencia-internacional-sobre-seguranca-fisica-nuclear
  - **Claim-level summary:** The Brazilian delegation to the Vienna conference reaffirmed commitment to the national nuclear-security architecture and said Brazil should resume efforts toward complete nuclear disarmament. This is strong evidence of good-faith support for security agreements.
  - **Question IDs:** `1B.4`; also `1B.3`, `1B.1`

- **Claim:** Brazil remained actively engaged with the IAEA in 2024 on nuclear oversight and cooperation.
  - **Title:** `AIEA reconhece papel "crucial" da CNEN no desenvolvimento da tecnologia nuclear no Brasil`
  - **Publisher:** Comissão Nacional de Energia Nuclear
  - **Date:** June 24, 2024
  - **Recoverable URL:** https://www.gov.br/cnen/pt-br/assunto/ultimas-noticias/aiea-reconhece-papel-crucial-da-cnen-no-desenvolvimento-da-tecnologia-nuclear-no-brasil
  - **Claim-level summary:** CNEN reported that IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi emphasized indispensable Brazilian cooperation and ongoing collaboration. That supports a picture of active, good-faith institutional engagement with inspection and verification norms.
  - **Question IDs:** `1B.4`; also `1B.3`

- **Claim:** Brazil participated in an IAEA regulatory self-assessment process in 2024.
  - **Title:** `Brasil participa de autoavaliação inédita da AIEA em Viena, contribuindo para o fortalecimento da segurança nuclear global`
  - **Publisher:** Comissão Nacional de Energia Nuclear
  - **Date:** October 3, 2024
  - **Recoverable URL:** https://www.gov.br/cnen/pt-br/assunto/ultimas-noticias/brasil-participa-de-autoavaliacao-inedita-da-aiea-em-viena-contribuindo-para-o-fortalecimento-da-seguranca-nuclear-global
  - **Claim-level summary:** Brazil took part in an IAEA regulatory self-assessment that focused on strengthening nuclear safety governance. This is indirect but relevant evidence of disciplined oversight and willingness to accept review.
  - **Question IDs:** `1B.4`; also `1B.3`

- **Claim:** Lula publicly pushed a Brazil-China peace formula for Ukraine centered on talks, de-escalation, and a ceasefire.
  - **Title:** `Brasil e China assinam proposta conjunta de negociação de paz para guerra da Ucrânia e Rússia`
  - **Publisher:** Reuters via UOL
  - **Date:** May 23, 2024
  - **Recoverable URL:** https://noticias.uol.com.br/ultimas-noticias/reuters/2024/05/23/brasil-e-china-assinam-proposta-conjunta-de-negociacao-de-paz-para-guerra-da-ucrania-e-russia.htm
  - **Claim-level summary:** The joint proposal said dialogue and negotiation were the only viable solution and called for conditions to resume direct talks and move toward a comprehensive ceasefire. This is direct de-escalation evidence and supports good-faith agreement-seeking.
  - **Question IDs:** `1B.4`; also `1B.1`

- **Claim:** Lula’s UN-level diplomacy in 2024 explicitly advocated Russia-Ukraine talks rather than escalation.
  - **Title:** `Lula at UN touts Brazil-China plan for Ukraine-Russia talks`
  - **Publisher:** Reuters via Investing.com
  - **Date:** September 24, 2024
  - **Recoverable URL:** https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/lula-at-un-says-brazil-china-propose-plan-for-ukrainerussia-talks-3630110
  - **Claim-level summary:** Reuters reported Lula advocating a plan for talks between Russia and Ukraine to end the war. This is consistent with support for de-escalation agreements, though the article notes Ukraine had already rejected the plan.
  - **Question IDs:** `1B.4`; also `1B.1`

### Counterevidence / cautions

- **Claim:** Ukraine rejected the Brazil-China peace initiative as lacking legitimacy and serving Russian interests.
  - **Title:** `Ukraine's Zelenskiy dismisses 'destructive' China-Brazil peace initiative`
  - **Publisher:** Reuters via Investing.com
  - **Date:** September 12, 2024
  - **Recoverable URL:** https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/ukraines-zelenskiy-dismisses-destructive-chinabrazil-peace-initiative-3612966
  - **Claim-level summary:** Zelenskiy said the initiative was “destructive,” complained Kyiv was not involved, and argued it lacked respect for Ukraine’s territorial integrity. This does not prove bad faith, but it is the strongest 2024 counterweight to the good-faith interpretation.
  - **Question IDs:** `1B.4`; also `1B.1`

### Search gap

I did **not** find reliable 2024 evidence that Lula:
- undermined arms-control or disarmament agreements,
- obstructed inspections or safeguards,
- or rejected multilateral nonproliferation processes.

The strongest 2024 evidence is on the positive side: disarmament delegation creation, nuclear-security conference participation, IAEA engagement, and repeated ceasefire/de-escalation advocacy. The main ambiguity is that the Brazil-China Ukraine initiative was criticized by Ukraine as insufficiently inclusive and overly aligned with Russia.
